descripcion_geo: Valley southwest of Jerusalem, between the city and Bethlehem. fertile land; battle scene between David and the Philistines.
importancia_estrategica: Battlefield between David and the Philistines; Its name (Rephaites = giants) evokes the pre-Israelite peoples.

historias.titulo: David's battles against Philistines in the valley
historias.descripcion: The Philistines are deployed in the valley of the Rephaim; David consults the Lord twice and defeats them.

historias.titulo: The harvest of the valley of the Rephaim in Isaiah
historias.descripcion: Isaiah uses the harvest of the valley of the Rephaim as an image of judgment: only a cluster will remain, like shaking an olive tree.

historias.titulo: The surprise attack of the sycamores
historias.descripcion: God orders David to attack the Philistines when he hears the sound of footsteps in the tops of the sycamore trees in the valley.

personajes.descripcion: He won two decisive battles against the Philistines in the valley of the Rephaim.
He used the valley as an image of the destruction of the north of Israel.
Giants that inhabited the valley before the arrival of Israel; His name persists as a toponym.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Valley of the Rephaim: relevant geographical region in the Old Testament.

judaismo.descripcion: God gives David a unique military signal: to attack when the noise sounds in the tops of the sycamores (2 Sam 5:24). Victory is miraculous, not tactical.
judaismo.significado_teologico: God gives David a unique military signal: to attack when the noise sounds in the tops of the sycamores (2 Sam 5:24). Victory is miraculous, not tactical.
